Welcome to Ark Dickens Academy
On behalf of our whole school community, I am delighted to welcome you to Ark Dickens Primary Academy. I am privileged to be Head of School at Ark Dickens Primary Academy where our motto is ‘Be your best’ and this reflects our ethos of ensuring every child is provided with every opportunity to reach their potential. Children are supported in becoming confident and independent young people, who thrive on challenge, and are motivated to learn. All schools have their own distinctive ‘feel’ which makes each one unique. We believe that the ‘special feel’ at Ark Dickens Primary comes from our caring, supportive, and friendly environment.

pageCache.text:
Welcome to Personal, Social, Health and Emotional Education (PSHE)
Why do we learn Personal, Social, Health and Emotional Education (PSHE)?
Pupils at Ark Dickens will leave the academy with the skills and knowledge to ‘Be your Best’ as a result of well-planned, engaging PHSE lessons.
Our children will leave as well-rounded individuals, who will be able to:
Make well informed decisions about safety and behaviour.
Understand the importance of physical activity and diet for a healthy lifestyle.
Apply a range of effective strategies in order to manage feelings and emotions.
Have healthy relationships built on trust and respect.
Understand and care for their bodies, building confidence and healthy habits.
Protect their personal information, recognise risks, and make responsible choices.
Use money wisely to make smart choices and plan for the future.
Prepare for and understand the physical and emotional changes they will experience as they grow.
Head of Department
Miss A Matthews
Our approach
In line with the National Curriculum Framework, knowledge and skills are embedded across all PSHE lessons and are constantly revisited throughout pupils’ time at Ark Dickens. Each half term centres around a key overarching focus—Understanding Myself, Self with Others, and Self Within the World—which is explored through a range of topics including Wellbeing, My Body and Me, Healthy Choices, Healthy Relationships, Identity and Community, Digital Lives, Aspiration and Money, and Transition. Each lesson is taught weekly by the class teacher, as they have the best relationship with their pupils, and are tailored to the needs of our pupils. We strive to provide our students with the knowledge, skills, and mindset they need to confidently step into the future. By preparing them to face challenges with determination and optimism, we nurture their ability to adapt and grow. This reflects our school’s core value of resilience—the strength to persevere through difficulties and emerge stronger.

Welcome to Art and Design Technology
Why do we learn art and design technology?
At Ark Dickens Primary Academy, we believe that art and design technology should spark imagination and creativity in every child. Our curriculum is designed to inspire pupils by helping them learn about famous artists and giving them the skills to create their own artwork with confidence.
Through a wide range of activities—like drawing, painting, and sculpture—children explore colour, shape, pattern, and space. They also learn how art and design technology has played an important role in different cultures and times.
In line with the national curriculum, our aim is for our children to enjoy and appreciate visual arts while developing their own creative ideas. They will:
Create their own artwork and express their thoughts and experiences
Learn key techniques in drawing, painting, sculpture, and design
Talk about and understand different types of art using the right vocabulary
Discover the work of great artists, designers, and craft makers from history and around the world
We want every child to be their best, feel confident and excited about expressing themselves through art and design technology.
Head of Department
Miss R Begum
Our approach
At Ark Dickens, our art and design technology lessons are carefully planned so that children build on their skills each year. They regularly practise drawing and painting, and they also explore sculpture, collage, and printing. This helps them grow in confidence and creativity over time.
Children use sketchbooks to record their ideas and practise techniques. These books help them revisit what they’ve learned and keep their creativity flowing.
Each unit begins with a close look at the work of a well-known artist. We choose artists whose work clearly shows the style or technique we’re focusing on. Children first learn about the artist’s work, then try out some of the same techniques themselves. This gives them a chance to practise before creating their own original pieces.
We also link Art and Design to other subjects like History, Geography, and Science. This helps children make connections in their learning and understand how art fits into the wider world.

Welcome to Religious Education
Why do we learn Religious Education?
Pupils at Ark Dickens will leave the academy with the skills and knowledge to ‘Be your Best’ as a result of well-planned, engaging lessons. As enquirers, they will be able to:
- Ask and respond to challenging questions about the meaning and purpose of beliefs.
- Explore their own beliefs be it either religious or non-religious.
- Show respect for different faiths and beliefs.
Head of Department
Miss B Lever
Our approach
In line with the National Curriculum Framework, knowledge is embedded across all R.E lessons and are constantly revisited throughout pupils’ time at Ark Dickens. Each unit of work has 5 key areas so that children gain a full understanding of the concept which they are studying:
- Communicate – What is my own response?
- Apply – How does the concept affect others?
- Enquire – What does the concept mean?
- Contextualise – How does this look in other religions?
- Evaluate – What value does the concept hold to others?
In each unit, one area is assessed so that across the year, children apply all skills and knowledge learnt.
Leaders at Dickens will ensure that staff are well equipped with the knowledge and skills to plan engaging lessons that will spark curiosity in all learners.
Parents/carers are able to withdraw their child from RE or collective worship.

Welcome to Music
Why do we learn music?
Pupils at Ark Dickens will leave the academy with the skills to ‘Be your Best’ as a result of well-planned, engaging lessons. In line with the National Curriculum and as musicians our pupils will
have access to high quality musical experiences that deliver life-enhancing benefits through curriculum and enrichment opportunities.
Encounter great music making, adopting habits and behaviours that foster a respectful and joyful community.
Experience a knowledge-led curriculum where they leave lessons gaining new knowledge and the ability to retain it.
Have their life beyond the school acknowledged and its importance reflected in enrichment opportunities.
In addition, children will develop their understanding of the history of music.
Head of Department
Miss T Woods
Our approach
In line with the National Curriculum Framework, skills are embedded across all music lessons and are constantly revisited throughout pupils’ time at Ark Dickens. We have an integrated approach to curriculum development, progressive instrumental and vocal learning for every child and weekly enrichment ensembles and opportunities to attend networks events across the school. Furthermore, Dickens' approach to learning is built upon four pillars:
1. A cumulative, knowledge-rich curriculum - Our curriculum is designed to introduce and secure key musical knowledge and skills in a sequential and connected manner.
2. Placing the voice at the heart of musical learning - For us, musical learning begins with the voice, and throughout our curriculum pupils develop their musicianship through singing activities that offer increasing levels of challenge and complexity. Musicianship skills are further developed in our KS2 instrumental programme where our curricula lead pupils to establish a secure playing technique, explore creative ideas and develop musical understanding.
3. Exploratory, play-based learning from the earliest moments - Our approach to teaching in the Early Years Foundation Stage integrates formal and free-flow learning to unlock imagination and creativity. From Key Stage 1 onwards, activities that stimulate more conscious learning are phased in, introducing pupils to the building blocks of music that shape the world around them.
4. Developing community-minded learners - Opportunities to teach and reflect on behaviours that will secure a safe and successful learning community are woven into schemes of work. Pupils experience
A musical diet that encourages the exploration of historical and contemporary issues and invites them to consider their own contribution to society.

Welcome to Computing
Why do we learn computing?
At Ark Dickens, we believe that as computing and the use of technology is an increasing part of life today, it is imperative that all pupils gain the confidence and ability that they need in this subject, to prepare them for the challenge of a rapidly developing and changing technological world. The use of ICT will enhance and extend children’s learning across the whole curriculum whilst developing motivation and social skills. At this academy, we want to produce independent learners who have the confidence to use a range of technology within a range of contexts thus preparing them to be competent participants in a digital world. Therefore, we strive to ensure that computing is not only taught as a pure subject each week and that opportunities for computing across the curriculum are well planned and enhance our computing offer
Head of Department
Our approach
Pupils at Ark Dickens will leave the academy with the skills and knowledge to ‘Be your Best’ as a result of well-planned, engaging lessons. As confident users of technology, they will be able to:
- Design, write and debug using a range of programs. - Use simple reading to explain algorithms. - Understand computer networks including the internet. - Use search technologies safely and effectively with the understanding of how results are ranked. - Select and combine a variety of software, choosing appropriate content in order to achieve a given goal. - Use technology safely, respectfully and responsibly; recognising acceptable/unacceptable behaviour; identifying a range of ways to report concerns about content and contact.

Welcome to Geography
Why do we learn geography?
Pupils at Ark Dickens will leave the academy with the skills and knowledge to ‘Be your Best’ as a result of well-planned, engaging lessons. As Geographers, they will be able to:
- Name and locate cities, counties and countries using maps and atlases.
- Understand geographical similarities and differences through the study of human and physical geography.
- Describe and understand key aspects of human and physical geography.
Head of Department
Mr T Hutchings
Our approach
In line with the National Curriculum Framework, skills are embedded across all geography lessons and are constantly revisited throughout pupils’ time at Ark Dickens. Each lesson starts with a leading question and this is what drives the teaching throughout. Across a unit, lessons will be constructed of the following to ensure they are purposeful and outcome driven:
- A 'throwback thinkers' session allowing children to recap previous learning.
- Key vocabulary and knowledge required to answer the leading question.
- Practical opportunities for application of knowledge and skills.
- Assessment for learning opportunities.
Throughout the unit, teachers assess key lesson knowledge using Subject on a Page heatmaps.
Leaders at Dickens will ensure that staff are well equipped with the knowledge and skills to plan engaging lessons that will spark curiosity in all learners.

Pupils at Ark Dickens will leave the academy with the skills and knowledge to ‘Be your Best’ as a result of well-planned, engaging lessons. As Historians, they will be able to:

Welcome to Maths
Maths at Ark Dickens
The Ark Dickens Mastery Curriculum prepares our learners to be the fluent, confident mathematicians of the 21st century. It equips them with the problem solving, language skills and growth mindset they need to flourish in higher education or in a career of their choice.
Our lessons engage, challenge and support all learners, to work through fluency, reasoning and problem-solving activities. Our curriculum supports our whole school focus on children having a strong number sense and being secure with the key fundamentals. We continue to nurture our pupils’ love of maths and develop their curiosity to express their mathematical thinking in eloquent, appropriate ways.
Concrete, Pictorial and Abstract (CPA) representations are embedded into the mastery approach and teaching and learning at Ark Dickens. This supports learners in verbalising their mathematical thinking, exploring and connecting concepts and deepening their understanding.
Concrete – Pupils have the opportunity to use concrete objects and manipulatives to help them to understand and explain concepts.
Pictorial – Pupils then build on this concrete approach by using pictorial representations which can then be used to reason and solve problems.
Abstract – With foundations firmly laid pupils can move to an abstract approach using numbers and key concepts with confidence.
At Ark Dickens, we also have an afternoon 'Maths Meeting'. The purpose of these meetings is to recall existing knowledge and embed into long term memory. We call this 'sticky knowledge'. These sessions are fast paced and ensure engagement and enjoyment of maths for all. To continue learning outside of the classroom, we have Times Table Rockstars and Mathletics for all key stage 1 and 2 to access on their digital devices as well as whole school maths themed days.
Head of Department
Mr L Clarke
Our approach
All lessons are carefully planned and adapted taking in to account all learners needs. At Ark Dickens, all children undertake half termly arithmetic assessments and termly assessments. These assessments are carefully analysed, and the data is used to inform planning for daily lessons, maths meetings and maths in order to effectively narrow gaps, consolidate learning and provide provision for those pupils who need it.
Within whole class maths lessons, our children are taught the importance of using accurate mathematical vocabulary and are encouraged to use this when explaining problem solving, partner talk and answering questions. Children are encouraged to represent and solve mathematical concepts in a variety of ways using concrete manipulatives, pictures and the abstract form, numbers and symbols. We understand that explicit modelling is key to our children’s success as mathematicians. When working independently, we ensure there is a secure understanding of the skill being taught through procedural practise before applying this with a range of problem-solving challenges. Where possible, we ensure real life contexts are given to deepen understanding and importance of mathematical concepts.

Welcome to Physical Education
Why do we learn physical education?
At Ark Dickens, we want all children to leave the academy as competent and successful sports persons. Situated in a built-up area of Portsmouth, we know the importance of living a healthy and active lifestyle. Physical and mental health, wellbeing and approaches are a key part of the academies approach to delivering the best possible education. All children should leave the academy with a good understanding of how to keep themselves healthy and fit, able to work to goals, compete healthily and with a strong understanding of their physiology and psychology in order to keep themselves healthy in all facets of their life.
Head of Department
Mr M McDade
Our approach
In line with the National Curriculum Framework, pupils are taught using a holistic approach to physical education teaching along two strands: Sports and Fitness. We have developed an exciting curriculum engaging children in a wide variety of regular physical activities, as well as giving children the knowledge and information they need to make healthy choices to live well balanced lives.
- Sport: Our sports strand inspires pupils to succeed and excel in a broad range of competitive sport and physical activities. Key skills such as throwing and catching, passing, dribbling and keeping possession are developed across the year groups.
- Fitness: The aim of the fitness programme is to ensure that pupils receive regular exercise activity. Lessons are designed to raise the heart rate and improve overall fitness, stamina and flexibility. Units across the year and across the school develop flexibility and strength, cardiovascular fitness and stamina.
Throughout the year different after school clubs take place, which have included football, bench ball and multi-sports skills. Each class receives two sessions of PE per week in addition to the 'daily mile' We work alongside local schools and attend regular inter-school competitions and tournaments. We assess all learning outcomes using Heatmaps and SOAPs (Subjective, Objective, Assessment, Plan).

Welcome to Reading
Why do we learn reading?
By the time children leave Ark Dickens Primary School pupils have transferable skills that ensure they are confident readers that can enjoy a range of texts. They can make their own decisions about different texts, they can talk confidently about their own interest, likes and dislikes. Through receiving high quality reading we create well-read, enthusiastic, insightful and knowledgeable readers that will continue as readers later in life. It is essential that by the end of their primary education, all pupils are able to read fluently, and with confidence and in any subject. We hope that we fulfil our school’s vision; ‘be your best’ in the next stage of their lives to enable them to contribute positively to their community.
Head of Department
Our approach
At Ark Dickens, pupils are exposed to different reading genres through a variety of well-considered and diverse texts to create a love of reading. Children also learn about the key grammatical features that make up the English language and how they as readers can use these features to develop their reading fluency and expression. We believe that all pupils should be given access to high quality literature and these books are linked to the half-termly topic, with the aim of supporting the development of vocabulary and knowledge of the topic. The curriculum has been developed to focus and build on several core areas. Our journey begins with the Read Write Inc. synthetic phonics programme in Early Years which progresses to in depth class and independent reading lessons when children are ready. Key reading skills are taught throughout our reading programme such as; fluency and expression, prediction, inference, sequence, and summarising texts that they have read. Our pupils are exposed to a range of reading opportunities from visits to our school library, buddy reading scheme, diverse class reads. Our home reading scheme provides pupils with ability matched book as well as an own choice book for pleasure.

Welcome to Science
Why do we learn science?
It is our vision to ensure that pupils at Ark Dickens leave the academy with the skills and knowledge to ‘Be your Best’ as a result of well-planned, engaging lessons. As Scientists, they will:
- Have the scientific knowledge and conceptual understanding through the specific disciplines of biology, chemistry and physics
- Understand the nature, processes and methods of science through different types of science enquiries that help them to answer scientific questions about the world around them.
Have the scientific knowledge required to understand the uses and implications of science, today and for the future
Head of Department
Mrs S Khanom
Our approach
In line with the National Curriculum Framework, knowledge and skills are embedded across all Science lessons and are constantly revisited throughout pupils’ time at Ark Dickens. Each lesson starts with the throwback thinkers, and this is what drives the teaching throughout. . Across a unit, lessons will be constructed of the following to ensure they are purposeful and outcome driven:
- A ‘do now’ which recaps or focuses on retention of previous learning.
- Key vocabulary and knowledge required to answer the leading question.
- Practical opportunities for application of knowledge and skills.
- Assessment for learning opportunities.
- Regular Assessments including SOAPs and heatmaps to identify gaps in knowledge and skills.
- At the end of the unit, pupils will be assessed on their learning through a range of outcome driven activities including exam style questions and investigations.
Leaders at Dickens will ensure that staff are well equipped with the knowledge and skills to plan engaging lessons that will spark curiosity in all learners.

Welcome to Writing
Why do we learn writing?
The impact on our children is clear: progress, sustained learning and transferrable skills. By the end of their journey at Ark Dickens Primary Academy our children leave with highly developed communication skills that they can take with them to secondary education and beyond. Success is not only achieved through children’s attainment, but through their engagement with, and enthusiasm for, the many English opportunities that have been provided throughout their time with us. Upon transition to secondary school, our children appreciate the joy and wonder of reading and are able to express preferences and opinions about the texts that they read. With the implementation of the writing journey being well established and taught thoroughly in both key stages, children become confident writers and by the time they are in Upper Key Stage 2, most genres of writing are familiar and the teaching can focus on creativity, writer’s craft, sustained writing and manipulation of grammar and punctuation skills.
Head of Department
Mr L Prior
Our approach
At Ark Dickens, communication skills are practised in each lesson, where talking with peers is a constant feature. English lessons, for all year groups, typically feature writing and help to develop pupils’ skills in grammar and spelling. Writing is frequently linked to topic work; this provides pupils with the opportunity to apply their writing skills in a variety of contexts. The sequence of learning draws from pupils’ initial mark making and the meaning they give to the marks they make. In EYFS, children learn synthetic phonics, which enables them to assign greater meaning to the marks they make, being able to write a grapheme at first and eventually moving on to simple sentences in relation to stories that they have learned. In Key Stage 1, these skills are further developed. A variety of genres and purposes are covered in Key Stage 1 and writing across the curriculum is expected to enable all the children to become a strong independent writer in all subjects. As they enter Key Stage 2, pupils continue to expand their knowledge of writing and the English language by developing more technically challenging grammar such as relative clauses, co-ordinating and subordinating conjunctions, using a variety of fronted adverbials. This enables pupils to be able to choose how to write for a variety of audiences whilst ensuring that their composition remains relevant to the genre type. As children develop a secure understanding and ability to independently apply their writing skills, they are further encouraged to write across the Key Stage 2 curriculum applying what they have learned to become an even better writer.

Special educational needs
We have high aspirations for all our learners, and are particularly committed to supporting our SEND learners to reach their full potential.
At Ark Dickens Primary Academy, we are committed to supporting the right of every child to have equal access to a broad and balanced education, regardless of the academic or physical ability. We understand and recognise that sometimes children require additional support to help them with their learning, tuition and a language enrichment programme.
When children’s needs are complex and require additional support, we work with external agencies such as Educational Psychologists, Specialist teachers and Speech and Language therapists to ensure our provision is effective. If additional targeted support is advised, this is planned for and referred to in each child’s Individual Learning Plan e.g. speech and language targeted support.
Our school setting prides itself for having a strong sense of community where all adults strive to know and understand each and every child both academically and as a person. When difficulties or concerns arise, we ensure that early intervention is put in place to close gaps in learning, provide appropriate emotional support and ensure full access to the curriculum for their year group.

Safeguarding

Welcome from our Designated Safeguarding Leads
Ark Dickens is a community and all those directly connected (staff, governors, parents, families, and pupils) have an essential role to play in making it safe and secure. We recognise our moral and statutory responsibility to safeguard and promote the welfare of all children with their best interests at the centre of our work.
Ark Dickens recognises the importance of providing an ethos and environment within school that will help children to feel safe, secure, and respected; encourage them to talk openly; and enable them to feel confident that they will be listened to. This ethos is underpinned by our school values. We are alert to the signs of abuse and neglect and follow our procedures to ensure that children receive effective support, protection, and justice.

Reporing a safeguarding concern
At Ark Dickens Primary Academy, pupils always have member of staff they can talk to if they have any problems or concerns. Ark Dickens Primary Academy work with many safeguarding partners and these offer additional reporting, help and advice for pupils and parents.
